title: Solo Sick-Day Check-In Pact
oneLiner: People who live alone create a non-creepy safety pact for missed check-ins, illness days, and emergency escalation.
theme: 외로움 / 건강 - solo living safety without shame or surveillance.
targetUser: Single-person households, solo expats, remote workers, adult children living away from parents, and friends caring for each other from afar.
keyUX: User defines normal routines, illness flags, trusted contacts, privacy boundaries, missed-check escalation, and comfort messages; the app simulates exactly what happens if they go quiet.
requiredUISections: Daily check-in status header with privacy level and next deadline
Illness-day quick mode with symptoms, supplies, and help threshold
Message preview for gentle nudge, concern, and emergency
False-alarm pause and travel mode controls
Shareable pact summary for friends or family
sourceSignals: S13 - Guardian, a viral check-in app for people living alone exposed fears around isolated death, solo living, and emergency contacts: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jan/20/chinese-app-are-you-dead-exposed-deepest-darkest-fears
stitchPrompt: Build a production-grade web app prototype called "Solo Sick-Day Check-In Pact" for people who live alone and want a gentle safety net. The first screen must be a working check-in pact workspace with a daily status header, routine pattern builder, illness-day quick mode, trusted contact escalation ladder, message previews, false-alarm pause controls, travel mode, and shareable pact summary. Use realistic sample data: Seoul studio apartment, missed morning check-in, mild fever, no nearby family, two trusted friends, privacy level set to low-detail, two-day escalation rule, and a travel pause ending tonight. Design direction: use the calm-consumer profile with soft emotionally steady surfaces, clear reassurance copy, large readable safety states, and one gentle accent for confirming the pact. Do not make a marketing landing page; the first screen must be the working app.
